note.en: Ghatotkacha beheads the rakshasa Alayudha in the night battle and casts the head before Duryodhana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CLXXVIII ('Then the mighty son of Bhimasena threw down the head of the slain Alayudha before Duryodhana')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Drona Parva Section CLXXVIII narrates the Ghatotkacha-Alayudha duel and states Bhimasena's son threw the slain Alayudha's head before Duryodhana.

note.en: Alayudha comes to Duryodhana unbidden, offering to fight the Pandavas for him.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Section CLXXVIII ('Alayudha, having come to Duryodhana of his own accord')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Drona Parva Section CLXXVIII records that Alayudha came to Duryodhana of his own accord to fight for the Kauravas.

note.en: Sunda and Upasunda are brothers born of the Daitya Nikumbha, inseparable until Tilottama divides them.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXI ('Unto this Nikumbha, were born two sons called Sunda and Upasunda')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXI states that two sons, Sunda and Upasunda, were born to the asura Nikumbha.

note.en: Sunda descends through his father Nikumbha from the line of Hiranyakasipu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXI ('Nikumbha, endued with great energy and strength was born in the race of the great Asura, Hiranyakasipu')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXI traces Sunda's father Nikumbha to the race of the asura Hiranyakasipu.

note.en: Sunda and Upasunda quarrel over Tilottama and slay each other, as Brahma had designed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIV ('She is my wife, and therefore your superior, said Sunda')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIV shows Sunda seizing Tilottama and the brothers slaying each other in wrath for her sake.

note.en: Upasunda contends with his brother over Tilottama and both die in the quarrel.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIV ('It was thus that Asuras, ever united and inspired by the same purpose slew each other in wrath for the sake of Tilottama')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIV closes Narada's tale with the two asuras slaying each other for Tilottama's sake.

note.en: Brahma has Viswakarman fashion Tilottama and names her, sending her to divide the asura brothers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Rajya-labha Parva, Section CCXIII ('the Grandsire bestowed upon her the name of Tilottama')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CCXIII has Brahma order Viswakarman to create the damsel and bestow on her the name Tilottama.

note.en: Bhima kills the rakshasa Kirmira who bars the Pandavas' path into the forest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Section XI ('Hearing the account of the slaughter in combat of Kirmira, that foremost of Rakshasas')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XI is the Kirmira-badha Parva, in which Vidura recounts Bhima's slaughter of Kirmira.

note.en: Kirmira names himself Baka's brother when he challenges the Pandavas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Kirmira-badha Parva, Section XI ('The Rakshasa thus addressed, answered Yudhishthira the just, saying, I am the brother of Vaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section XI has the rakshasa declare to Yudhishthira that he is the brother of Vaka.

note.en: Madhu and Kaitabha are the paired primordial Daityas destroyed together by Vishnu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII narrates Madhu and Kaitabha acting as a pair and being beheaded together by Vishnu's discus.

note.en: Vishnu beheads Kaitabha with his discus after the pair grant him the boon of their own deaths.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII states the Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus.

note.en: Vishnu beheads Madhu with his discus in the same act that ends Kaitabha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCII ('the illustrious Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCII states the Deity cut off the heads of Madhu and Kaitabha with his keen-edged discus.

note.en: Dhundhu, the asura buried in the sea of sands, is reckoned the son of Madhu and Kaitabha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCIII ('The illustrious Dhundhu, O king, was the son of Madhu and Kaitabha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCIII opens by naming Dhundhu the son of Madhu and Kaitabha.

note.en: Dhundhu is named the son of Madhu and Kaitabha, and remembers his father's death at Vishnu's hands.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Markandeya-Samasya Parva, Section CCIII ('The illustrious Dhundhu, O king, was the son of Madhu and Kaitabha')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Vana Parva Section CCIII names Dhundhu the son of Madhu and Kaitabha, remembering his father's death at Vishnu's hands.

note.en: Sthulakesa finds Menaka's abandoned infant, names her Pramadvara and rears her as her foster-father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('the great Brahmana, Sthulakesa, the first of Munis, seeing that female child, and filled with compassion, took it up and reared it')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII has Sthulakesa take up and rear the forsaken child, name her Pramadvara, and betroth her to Ruru as her foster-father.

note.en: Ruru weds Pramadvara after giving her half his own life to recall her from death by snakebite.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('her foster-father betrothed the virgin Pramadvara to Ruru')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII records Sthulakesa betrothing Pramadvara to Ruru, and Ruru begetting a son on her as his wife.

note.en: Sunaka is born to Ruru and Pramadvara.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('And Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII states Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka.

note.en: Pramadvara is Sunaka's mother.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section VIII ('And Ruru begot on his wife Pramadvara a son called Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section VIII states the son Sunaka was begotten on Ruru's wife Pramadvara.

note.en: Ruru stands in the Bhrigu line running through Chyavana, in whose genealogy his son Sunaka is listed.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva, Section V ('And to Ruru also by his wife Pramadvara, was born a son, whose name was Sunaka')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section V gives the Bhrigu genealogy in which Chyavana's line runs down to Ruru and his son Sunaka.

note.en: Sringin is the son of the silent ascetic Samika, whose insult he avenges with a curse.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLII ('Samika repeatedly asked his son to save thee, but there is none to falsify his son's curse')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XLII has Samika speak of Sringin as his son and of his son's irrevocable curse.

note.en: Sringin curses Parikshit to die of Takshaka's bite within seven days for insulting his father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XLI ('Seven days hence, Takshaka, the lord of snakes, shall take the sinful king to the horrible abode of Death')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XLI records Sringin's curse that Takshaka would take the king to death in seven days.

note.en: Parikshit hangs a dead snake on the silent Samika's shoulder, the affront that provokes Sringin's curse.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Astika Parva, Section XL ('the king in anger thereupon placed upon his shoulder a dead snake, taking it up with the end of his bow')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section XL narrates Parikshit placing a dead snake on the meditating Samika's shoulder.

note.en: Kanwa rears the foundling Shakuntala in his hermitage and she names him her father.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXI ('I am the daughter of the virtuous, wise, high-souled, and illustrious ascetic Kanwa')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXI has Shakuntala tell Dushmanta that she is the daughter of the ascetic Kanwa.

note.en: Dushyanta comes to Kanwa's hermitage seeking the sage and finds Shakuntala there instead.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section LXXI ('I have come to worship the highly-blessed Rishi Kanwa')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section LXXI has Dushmanta arrive at the asylum declaring he came to worship the Rishi Kanwa.

note.en: Rama severs Dushana's arms and kills him in the battle of Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXVI ('like a mighty elephant whose husks have fallen off, Dushana, on his arms having been severed, fell down to the earth')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXVI narrates Rama cutting off Dushana's two arms and Dushana falling slain on the field.

note.en: Dushana is Khara's general at Janasthana, commanding his fourteen thousand rakshasas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXII ('Khara spoke unto his general, named Dushana, saying, Do thou, O gentle one, array fourteen thousand of those Rakshasas')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXII has Khara address Dushana as his general and order him to array the host.

note.en: Surpanakha names Khara and Dushana among Ravana's brothers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XVII ('the brothers Khara and Dushana renowned in conflict (are also my brothers)')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XVII has Surpanakha list Khara and Dushana among her and Ravana's brothers.

note.en: Rama splits the head of Khara's general Mahakapala in the Janasthana battle.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXVI ('Raghu's son split Mahakapala's head... and they fell down to the earth like mighty trees of many boughs')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXVI states Raghu's son split Mahakapala's head and the three generals fell to earth.

note.en: Rama shoots out Sthulakshya's eyes and the rakshasa falls dead at Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXVI ('lodged the eyes of Sthulakshya with sharp shafts. And they fell down to the earth like mighty trees of many boughs')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXVI has Rama pierce Sthulakshya's eyes with sharp shafts before he falls to earth.

note.en: Rama kills Pramathi, one of three rakshasa generals who rush him together at Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXVI ('afflicted Pramathi with countless shafts... And they fell down to the earth like mighty trees of many boughs')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXVI names Pramathi among the three generals Rama afflicted with shafts until they fell dead.

note.en: Mahakapala is one of Khara's four foremost captains at Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXIII ('And Mahakapala, Sthulaksha, Pramathi and Triciras... posted themselves around Khara')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXIII lists Mahakapala among the four who went before the forces around Khara.

note.en: Sthulakshya is one of Khara's four foremost captains at Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXIII ('And Mahakapala, Sthulaksha, Pramathi and Triciras... posted themselves around Khara')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXIII lists Sthulaksha among the four captains stationed around Khara.

note.en: Pramathi is one of Khara's four foremost captains at Janasthana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XXIII ('And Mahakapala, Sthulaksha, Pramathi and Triciras... posted themselves around Khara')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XXIII lists Pramathi among the four who went at the back of Dushana around Khara.

note.en: Rama and Lakshmana sever Kavandha's arms, felling the headless demon who then directs them to Sugriva.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section LXX ('Rama, stationed on the right side, cut off in no time its right arm with his dagger and the heroic Lakshmana, the left one')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section LXX has Rama cut off Kavandha's right arm and Lakshmana the left, after which the demon falls.

note.en: Lakshmana cuts off Kavandha's left arm as Rama takes the right.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section LXX ('the heroic Lakshmana, the left one. Having got its arms dissevered, the terrible-voiced, Kavandha, of huge arms... fell flat on the ground')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section LXX states Lakshmana severed Kavandha's left arm, after which the demon fell flat on the ground.

note.en: The ascetic Sthulashira curses Kavandha to keep his monstrous form.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section LXXI ('assuming this terrible shape I assailed and enraged the great ascetic Sthulashira... Thereupon he imprecated curses upon me, saying Do thou retain this ghastly shape')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section LXXI has Kavandha recount enraging Sthulashira, who cursed him to retain his ghastly shape.

note.en: Rama seeks out Sarabhanga in Dandaka, and the sage sends him on to Sutikshna before entering the fire.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section V ('This dense forest is hard to live in... Therefore will we speedily repair to the ascetic Sarabhanga. Thereupon Raghava set out for the hermitage of Sarabhanga')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section V narrates Rama going to Sarabhanga's hermitage and the sage directing him onward.

note.en: Sarabhanga directs Rama onward to the ascetic Sutikshna.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section V ('O Rama, here in this forest lives a pious and self-restrained ascetic of mighty energy, named Sutikshna. He will bring about thy good')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section V has Sarabhanga name Sutikshna to Rama and give him the road to his hermitage.

note.en: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana stay with the ascetic Sutikshna in the Dandaka forest.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section VII ('Rama accompanied by his brother as well as Sita went to the asylum of Sutikshna in company with the twice-born ones')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section VII narrates Rama going with Sita and Lakshmana to Sutikshna's asylum.

note.en: Savari served Matanga's disciples at his asylum and waits there for Rama after they depart.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section LXXIII ('the disciples of the great ascetic Matanga lived there... there liveth an immortal mendicant woman, by name Savari, who had waited in attendance upon those departed ones')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section LXXIII describes Matanga's asylum, his disciples, and Savari who attended upon them.

note.en: Rama and Lakshmana pass through Matanga's wood on the way to Pampa.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section LXIX ('passing by the forest of Krauncha the two brothers descried on their way the asylum of Matanga')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section LXIX has Rama and Lakshmana descry the asylum of Matanga on their search for Sita.

note.en: Ravana compels the reluctant Maricha to take the golden-deer form that draws Rama away from Sita.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XLIV ('And remembering the words of Ravana, the Rakshasa reflected, By what means can Sita send away Lakshmana, and Ravana carry off Sita staying in solitude?')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XLIV shows the dying Maricha executing Ravana's instruction to cry in Rama's voice.

note.en: Rama's arrow kills Maricha in his golden-deer disguise, and the dying rakshasa cries out in Rama's voice.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XLIV ('that best of arrows, like unto a thunderbolt, deeply pierced the breast of Maricha, wearing the shape of a deer')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XLIV states Rama's arrow pierced the breast of Maricha in deer form, and he gave up his life.

note.en: Maricha's deer illusion lures Rama from the hermitage and enables Ravana's abduction of Sita.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XLIV ('Maricha wearing the shape of a deer, showing himself and disappearing from sight, drew Raghava a long way from the hermitage')

verification.notes: Dutt's Aranya Kanda Section XLIV narrates Maricha as the deer drawing Rama far from the hermitage where Sita waited.

note.en: Durdhasa is one of five commanders Ravana sends against Hanuman at the gate of the Ashoka grove.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sundara Kanda, Section XLVI ('Durdhasa discharged at Hanuman's head five white iron arrows with yellow heads')

verification.notes: Dutt's Sundara Kanda Section XLVI has Durdhasa shoot five arrows at Hanuman's head among the five leaders Ravana directed.

note.en: Ravana names Durdhasa among five foremost commanders sent to seize Hanuman.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sundara Kanda, Section XLVI ('he directed five of the foremost leaders of his forces, the heroic Virupaksha, Yupaksha, the Rakshasa Durdharsha, Praghasa, and Masakarna')

verification.notes: Dutt's Sundara Kanda Section XLVI lists Durdharsha among the five leaders Ravana directed against Hanuman.

note.en: Sarana and Shuka are Ravana's paired counsellors, sent together to spy on the monkey host.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Yuddha Kanda, Section XXV ('the graceful Ravana addressed his two counsellors, Suka and Sarana')

verification.notes: Dutt's Yuddha Kanda Section XXV names Suka and Sarana together as Ravana's two counsellors.

note.en: Ravana commissions Sarana to enter the monkey host in disguise and count its strength.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Yuddha Kanda, Section XXV ('Being thus commissioned, these heroes, the Rakshasas, Suka and Sarana, assuming monkey-shapes, entered into the hosts of monkeys')

verification.notes: Dutt's Yuddha Kanda Section XXV has Ravana commission Sarana, who takes monkey-shape and enters the host.

note.en: Shatananda is Janaka's officiating priest, set before the king when Vishwamitra brings Rama to Mithila.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section L ('placing the priests Satananda before him, as well as the high-souled family priests, speedily taking the arghya, at once went out in humble guise')

verification.notes: Dutt's Bala Kanda Section L places Satananda at the head of Janaka's priests as the king receives Vishwamitra.

note.en: Shatananda questions Vishwamitra about Ahalya's restoration and then recounts Vishwamitra's own history to Rama.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section LI ('Hearing those words of his, the mighty ascetic Vicwamitra, skilled in speech, replied unto Satananda... the ascetic's wife hath been united with him, even as Renuka with Bhrigu's son')

verification.notes: Dutt's Bala Kanda Section LI records the exchange between Satananda and Vishwamitra over the ascetic's wife.

note.en: Shatananda narrates Vishwamitra's rise to brahmarshihood before Rama and Lakshmana at Mithila.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section LXV ('Hearing Satananda's narration delivered in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana, Janaka with clasped hands addressed the son of Kucika')

verification.notes: Dutt's Bala Kanda Section LXV closes Satananda's narration delivered in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana.

note.en: Gargya is among the eastern sages who come to congratulate Rama on regaining his kingdom.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Uttara Kanda, Section I ('Kaucika, and Yavakrita, and Gargya, and Galava, and Kanva - son unto Madhalithi - who dwelt in the east, (came thither)')

verification.notes: Dutt's Uttara Kanda Section I lists Gargya among the ascetics of the east who came to Rama after the rakshasas were slain.

note.en: A sage Dhaumya is listed among the western ascetics who come to Rama's court after the war.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Uttara Kanda, Section I ('And Nrishadgu, and Kahashi, and Dhaumya, and that mighty sage Kauceya who abode in the western quarter, came there accompanied by their disciples')

verification.notes: Dutt's Uttara Kanda Section I names Dhaumya among the sages of the western quarter who came with their disciples.

note.en: Galava serves Vishwamitra for a hundred years and insists on paying a preceptor's fee.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Section CVI ('Thus commanded by his preceptor, Galava, highly pleased, said in a sweet voice unto Viswamitra... What final gift shall I make thee in consequence of thy services as preceptor?')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Udyoga Parva Section CVI has Galava wait upon Viswamitra and address him as his preceptor when dismissed.

note.en: Garuda carries his friend Galava across the quarters in the search for the eight hundred white steeds.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Section CVII ('And while Galava was thus lamenting, his friend Garuda, the son of Vinata, appeared in his sight... Thou art a dear friend of mine')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Udyoga Parva Section CVII has Garuda appear to the lamenting Galava and name him a dear friend.

note.en: Dhaumya becomes the household priest of the Pandavas on the Gandharva's advice.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Chaitraratha Parva, Section CLXXXV ('the Pandavas going to Utkochaka, the sacred asylum of Dhaumya installed Dhaumya as their priest')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CLXXXV narrates the Pandavas going to Utkochaka and installing Dhaumya as their priest.

note.en: Arjuna's question to the Gandharva Angaraparna leads the Pandavas to Dhaumya.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Chaitraratha Parva, Section CLXXXV ('Arjuna asked, O Gandharva... Tell us, therefore, which Veda-knowing Brahmana is worthy to be appointed as our priest. The Gandharva replied... Dhaumya, the younger brother of Devala')

verification.notes: Ganguli's Adi Parva Section CLXXXV records Arjuna asking for a priest and the Gandharva naming Dhaumya.
